page_title: Building Blockchain in Go. Part 1: Basic Prototype - Going the distance

summary.title: Building Blockchain in Go. Part 1: Basic Prototype
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a minimal blockchain in Go: hashed blocks linked into a back-linked chain with a genesis block.
takeaways: A block holds timestamp, data, previous block hash, and its own hash; the hash is SHA-256 over the concatenated fields.
A blockchain is an ordered, back-linked list; the prototype stores blocks in a Go slice.
A chain must start with a genesis block, so the constructor creates one before any blocks are added.
The prototype omits proof-of-work, consensus, and transactions, which the author says are covered in later parts.
summary.summary: The article is Part 1 of a series building a simplified cryptocurrency in Go. It defines a Block struct with Timestamp, Data, PrevBlockHash and Hash fields, computes the hash with SHA-256 over the concatenated fields, and adds a NewBlock constructor. It then wraps blocks in a Blockchain type backed by a slice, adds an AddBlock method, and creates a genesis block, printing the chain as a demo. The author notes what is missing: proof-of-work, consensus, and real transactions.
